thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change on the VPC cluster we saw a 2.7x tail-latency spike for short-chat requests (<= 64 tokens). Profiling attached. :eyes:

maria: link to perf graph: https://perf.redwood/internal/plot/abcd1234 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: Top-level finding: continuous-batching now forms fewer micro-batches because `token_budget` heuristic is lower when kv-cache hits are high. That made per-token kernel choice favor small-block GEMMs -> higher kernel overhead.

chris: Hmm, so KV cache hitrate improvement _reduced_ batching packing? That sounds backwards.

alex: Yeah — our heuristic computes effective_remaining_tokens = (request_window - cached_prefix) and then tries to pack until token_budget. With KV hits, cached_prefix grows so effective_remaining small -> we flush earlier.

maria: Can you paste the snippet of the current heuristic?

alex:
```
# simplified
effective_tokens = max(request.max_tokens - kv_cache.prefix_len, 1)
if effective_tokens < token_budget_threshold:
    emit_batch()
else:
    continue_accumulating()
```

ryan: For private deployments we allow overrides in `private.yaml` per-node. Proposed quick fix: cap kv_cache influence and add `min_continuous_budget` default 64.

devops: what's the doh impact on latency if we cap at 64?

alex: Local sim (qps=120) -> p95 drops from 220ms to 140ms, cost +3% due to slightly larger batches. Tail improved a lot.

chris: Any effect on kernel selection? We want to steer kernels toward batch-friendly paths.

alex: Yes — with min budget 64 we force compile path to choose medium-block GEMMs for sequence length 32/64 which have better amortized setup.

sre-bot: INCIDENT-#2319 created (priority=P2) — tagging eng-runtime, eng-infra.

maria: Implementation plan:
- add `min_continuous_budget` config in private.yaml + console override
- add `kv_weight` param (0..1) to shrink kv influence
- add telemetry counter `batch_formation.reason` (kv_hit|timeout|budget)
- run canary in one VPC region

chris: +1. For canary, recommend VPC nodes with worst-case constrained CPU (n1-standard-2 equiv) to exercise kernel overhead.

devops: I'll add the flag to the private helm chart and create a migration note. Example override:
```
continuous_batching:
  min_budget: 64
  kv_weight: 0.5
  max_wait_ms: 25
```

ryan: Also watch `kv_inflight_pct` metric — some models saw increased KV lock contention when we increased batching.

alex: Good call — we'll add a short-circuit: if kv_inflight_pct > 0.6, lower batching window.

maria: Timeline? Can we have a canary tomorrow and rollback plan?

alex: I'll push a small PR today with tests and perf script. Devops can deploy canary in `vpc-eu-west-2` tomorrow morning. Rollback via chart flag flip.

chris: Nice. Also file a follow-up to revisit kernel-selector thresholds — we might add a simple cost model: setup_cost vs per_token_cost to choose kernel at batch-formation time.

alex: Agreed. I'll drop a short doc in eng-runtime/notes with sim graphs.

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: 2026-03-14T09:00Z (canary) — watchers: @eng-runtime, @eng-infra

maria: :thumbsup: Thanks — this should help our private customers on constrained boxes.

alex: If anyone wants to repro locally, run `tools/perf/run_sim.sh --qps 120 --kv-hit 0.8 --budget 64` and look at `perf/out/*`.

chris: Great thread. Keep updates here.
